subject.title: Telegram owner commands: trusted execution mode for approval-gated actions

question: Should OpenClaw add a trusted-owner approval-bypass mode for Telegram group-origin privileged actions, and if so should it be a shared approval/elevated policy instead of a Telegram-only boolean?
rationale: The requested behavior intentionally skips approval prompts for privileged group-chat actions and adds config surface, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent security boundary or product semantics.

options.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

options.title: Keep Current Approval Model
options.body: Decline the bypass and document that operators who want no prompts should use existing elevated-full behavior only when host policies are already permissive.

options.title: Add Telegram-Only Shortcut
options.body: Implement the proposed Telegram setting directly, accepting a smaller surface with higher risk of policy drift from shared approvals and elevated execution.

recommendation.title: Design Shared Trusted-Owner Policy
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default policy with explicit sender, allowlisted group, tool-class, destructive-operation, audit, docs, and regression-test semantics across the approval stack.

likelyOwner.reason: The open choice is primarily product/security boundary direction, and Peter's recent approval/security policy history is the clearest routing signal for that decision.
